# prism-kappa Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Kappa: Decides whether one object may enter the Prism under its kappa label, the content address of UOR-Foundation/kappa-registry (feat/rewrite-after-poc, commit 618f477745e601f1bf1bd5cc62aed6fea4c8936d): an axis name, a colon and the digest in lowercase hex. A label is read as kappa-registry's Kappa::parse reads it, and an object is admitted only when the browser re-derived the very digest the label names.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always nocolon when colon is absent

The app SHALL answer `nocolon` when colon is absent, because a label without its colon names no axis (KappaParseError::NoColon).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `absent other wrong bad match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nocolon`
- **AND** the app answers `nocolon`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always unknownaxis when colon is present and axis is other

The app SHALL answer `unknownaxis` when colon is present and axis is other, because only kappa-registry's six axes are content addresses (KappaParseError::UnknownAxis).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `present other wrong lower match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `unknownaxis`
- **AND** the app answers `unknownaxis`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never admit when digits is wrong

The app SHALL NOT answer `admit` when digits is wrong, because a digest of the wrong length for its axis is no address on it (KappaParseError::WrongDigitCount).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `present sha256 wrong lower match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `admit`
- **AND** the app answers `digits`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never unverified when digits is wrong

The app SHALL NOT answer `unverified` when digits is wrong, because a digest of the wrong length for its axis is no address on it (KappaParseError::WrongDigitCount).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `present sha256 wrong lower match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `unverified`
- **AND** the app answers `digits`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never admit when hex is bad

The app SHALL NOT answer `admit` when hex is bad, because the wire form is lowercase hex only; any other digit refuses (KappaParseError::BadHex).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `present sha256 right bad match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `admit`
- **AND** the app answers `badhex`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never unverified when hex is bad

The app SHALL NOT answer `unverified` when hex is bad, because the wire form is lowercase hex only; any other digit refuses (KappaParseError::BadHex).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **AND** the app answers `badhex`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Otherwise admit

The app SHALL answer `admit` when no rule matches, because Prism Kappa: the decision tree's path that meets no test.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `present sha256 right lower match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `admit`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `absent other wrong bad match` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `nocolon`, decided by REQ-001, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 5 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `admit`, `unverified`, `mismatch`, `collision`, `nocolon`, `unknownaxis`, `digits`, `badhex`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `colon` | `present`, `absent` | whether the label has the colon that separates its axis from its digest |
| `axis` | `sha256`, `sha512`, `blake3`, `sha1`, `sha3x256`, `keccak256`, `other` | the axis the label names before its colon, one of kappa-registry's six, or anything else |
| `digits` | `right`, `wrong` | whether the digest has exactly twice its axis's digest length in hex digits |
| `hex` | `lower`, `bad` | whether every digest digit is lowercase hex (0-9, a-f) |
| `digest` | `match`, `mismatch`, `uncomputed`, `collision` | the one word the request carries: the browser re-derived the label's digest from the object's bytes (match), derived another (mismatch), could not derive it on this host (uncomputed), or found a SHA-1 collision |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `admit` | the object enters under its label |
| `unverified` | the label is well formed, its digest not derived here |
| `mismatch` | the object's bytes derive another digest |
| `collision` | the digest is a known SHA-1 collision |
| `nocolon` | the label has no axis separator |
| `unknownaxis` | the axis is not one of kappa-registry's six |
| `digits` | the digest has the wrong length for its axis |
| `badhex` | the digest is not lowercase hex |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 5 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `present sha256 right lower match` gives `admit`
- `present sha256 right lower mismatch` gives `mismatch`
- `present sha256 right lower uncomputed` gives `unverified`
- `present sha256 right bad match` gives `badhex`
- `present sha256 wrong lower match` gives `digits`
- `absent other wrong bad match` gives `nocolon`
- `present other wrong lower match` gives `unknownaxis`
- `present blake3 right lower uncomputed` gives `unverified`
- `present sha1 right lower collision` gives `collision`
- `present sha1 right lower uncomputed` gives `unverified`
- `present sha3x256 right lower uncomputed` gives `unverified`
- `present keccak256 right lower uncomputed` gives `unverified`
- `present sha512 right lower match` gives `admit`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
